summary:
No live signal to chase today — every recent-form window across R1 through R4 reads 0-0 (n=0) on both the rating×category trends and the strong-play unit P/L tracker. That's not a cold streak, that's an empty sample: we're in the dead window with no games on the board, so there's nothing on today's slate to cross-reference against hot or cold combos. Any "trend" talk right now would be fabricated — the last real signal in the log is 30+ days stale, and none of the four ratings have logged a decision in the 7d, 14d, or 30d buckets. Until games resume, lean entirely on season-long structure rather than anything billed as current heat.

That structure still tells you where to point the model when action returns. Trends remains the engine across all four ratings — R1-R3 all sit at 629-489 (56%, n=1118) on trends alone, and it's the anchor in every top category combo: trends+sp leads at 58.0% (370-268, n=638), with trends+runs (57.3%, n=705) and trends+bullpen (56.8%, n=688) close behind. Bullpen_fatigue is the one stat to fade across the board — R1-R4 all sit under 50% on it (R4 worst at 45%, 203-244), so any pick that's strong only because of a bullpen_fatigue read deserves a discount. On team trust, LAD is the headline: 39-17 (70%) when picked, and a monster 28-7 (80%, +27.0u) in strong-play spots — the best combination of volume and strong-play edge in the data. TBR (70%, n=63, strong +21.0u) and BOS (70%, n=56, strong 76%/+19.0u) sit right behind. NYY is the one name to treat skeptically regardless of rating: 49% straight (23-24) and a losing strong-play record at 39% (9-14, -4.0u) — when the model likes a Yankees game, don't assume the lean is live. R3 remains the top overall rating for bankroll purposes at 58% season-wide with +92.0u across 462 strong plays, narrowly ahead of R1 (+84.0u) and R2 (+81.0u), while R4's smaller sample still shows the best rate at 64% (119-68, +63.0u) — worth weighting heavier once it starts generating volume again.
